caption: What if you were a chipkali for a day? You'd walk up walls and across the ceiling with no glue. Your toes carry millions of microscopic hairs, each splitting into hundreds of tinier tips that grip using weak atom-level forces. In theory, all those hairs could hold two adults. To let go, you peel your toes like tape: a running gecko sticks and unsticks about 15 times a second. Your one weakness is dry Teflon, which geckos can barely grip. With no eyelids, you'd lick your eyes clean. A house gecko can eat up to 50 insects a day, and a dropped tail keeps wriggling while you escape, then regrows in months. Scientists copied gecko feet into an index-card-sized pad that held about 300 kg on glass. Plot twist: a chipkali in your dal is not poison, but it can carry Salmonella germs, so throw the food out. Would YOU swap with a chipkali for a day? 👇
